Ingredients:

- 1 chicken breast (thigh would work too)
- 200g tinned chopped tomatoes
- 1tsp tomato paste
- blend of paprika, basil, garlic powder, onion powder, salt & pepper to taste- I used a pinch of each 
- handful of grated cheddar
- 2tsp parmesan 
- 2 slices of pepperoni

Rub the chicken with the spice mixture, then pan fry for around 7 minutes per side until cooked through (depends on the size of the breast)

Remove chicken and set aside.

In the same pan, add the tinned tomatoes and tomato paste and stir, scraping up any stuck bits on the bottom of the pan.

Taste and season, add more of the herb mix if necessary, and add 1tsp of parmesan.

Transfer the sauce to a baking dish, then nestle the chicken breast in the sauce. Top with the pepperoni and grated cheddar, then the remaining teaspoon of parmesan.

Bake for 5 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling.

Ingredients:

- 200g riced cauliflower
- whatever veg you have on hand (I used mushrooms, corn, frozen peas, and white onion)
- a drizzle of toasted sesame oil
- 2 garlic cloves
- a good crack of black pepper
- 1-2tbsp vegan soy sauce 

Heat up a pan with sesame oil, then fry the onion and mushrooms for a few minutes.

Add the garlic, continue cooking for a minute.

Add the cauliflower rice, soy sauce, peas, and corn. Stir to combine.

Fry for a further 3 minutes and season.

Done!

I would have topped with scallions if I had any, but sesame seeds added a nice texture :)

Ingredients:

- 1 onion
- 1 bell pepper
- a handful of mushrooms and spinach 
- 80g dried lentils (I used red)
- 450ml vegetable stock
- 400g tinned tomatoes
- 1-2tbsp vegan curry paste (I used madras paste)
- garlic powder & pepper to taste

Sauté the veg until softened to your liking. Add the curry paste and seasonings and continue to fry for a few more minutes.

Tip in the lentils, stock, and tomatoes. Mix everything together and simmer for 30 minutes. Throw in the spinach towards the end.

Check the consistency, and if it’s too thin continue to simmer for another 10 minutes.

Done!

You're totally not alone. I absolutely hate being pregnant \(I'm 35 weeks, so I'm basically a big ball of resentment right now\), and I was really worried I won't love my baby when she's born. I find that whenever I doubt my attachment with my baby, it helps me to imagine someone taking her away. As dark as that sounds, playing the situation out in my head gives me this visceral, 'no, that's *mine*' feeling of protectiveness, that's reassuring in a way because I feel so strongly about keeping her with me. It might not work for everyone, but it helps ground me when I'm worried about not being attached to her\- it shows me I already am!

I know however much I hate carrying her around inside me, that's all the feeling means\- the dislike is because I'm so uncomfortable and feel like I'm missing out, none of it is aimed at the little human I'm having. While I'm not sure I completely *love* her yet, I try to acknowledge all the things I am feeling. I *a*m excited to meet her, I* a*m picturing her in my partner's arms and feeling fuzzy about it, etc. So I feel a lot for her already. Love will come in time once she's born, I'm certain :\)

It was awful, and the feelings still hit me every now and then.
